title: RETRACTED -- a fleet root that does not exist was claimed to scan as empty; the census already names it ABSENT
body:
## Tags

fleet, census, false-signal, silent-failure, retracted

## RETRACTED -- THIS ISSUE WAS NOT A DEFECT, AND THE RETRACTION LIVES HERE BECAUSE THIS IS WHERE A READER MEETS IT

**The claim below was false when filed on 2026-08-29 and was closed the same day.** It sat for five days stating a defect against a control that already existed, because `intent issues` had no edit verb and the retraction could only be written somewhere else. The verb landed; this is the correction, put where the claim is.

**What the issue claimed:** that a fleet root which does not exist is walked, yields nothing, and is indistinguishable from a root that genuinely holds no installs.

**Why it is false.** `render_doc` marks a missing root `-- ABSENT on this machine` in the document's own Roots-scanned section, and `fleet.bats` carries *an absent root is named as absent rather than silently dropped*, which passes. Re-verified 2026-09-03: `bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:279` emits the marker and the named test is green. Line numbers move -- it was `:246` when first cited -- so re-derive by grepping `ABSENT` rather than by opening the line.

**How the claim was produced, which is the part worth keeping.** `fleet_roots` and `find_installs` were read, neither contains an existence check, and the conclusion was written from that. The check lives in a third function that was never read. The Reproduction section below was then written **in the voice of something observed** -- *"exits 0 and prints the other root's estates"*, *"the document still LISTS the missing root"* -- having run neither. Both sentences are wrong: the document lists the root AND names it absent.

**So this is a defect claim filed against a control the filer had built, tested, and forgotten.** Reading two functions is not reading a code path, and prose written in the observed voice inherits the authority of a measurement without any measurement behind it.

## The original filing, kept verbatim below this line so the record is not tidied

## Summary

`fleet_roots` names two roots by default. A root that does not exist on disk is walked by `find`, yields nothing, and the scan continues -- so an entire root's worth of estates disappears from the census and **nothing in the output distinguishes that from a root that genuinely holds no installs.**

This is not hypothetical. It is live right now: the default list names `$HOME/Dropbox/Geodica/_tools`, and that directory no longer exists.

## Reproduction

**FALSE -- NEITHER SENTENCE WAS RUN. See the retraction above.**

Point `DEVBIN_FLEET_ROOTS` at a path that does not exist, alone or beside a real one. `fleet audit` exits 0 and prints the other root's estates. `fleet doc` writes a complete-looking document, whose "Roots scanned" section still LISTS the missing root -- so the document positively asserts it looked somewhere it did not look.

## Root Cause

**WRONG -- the check exists, in a function this analysis never read.**

`fleet_roots` emits paths and nothing validates them. `find_installs` walks whatever it is handed. There is no existence check anywhere on the path.

## Impact

**The general lesson survives its false instance and is why this issue is corrected rather than deleted.** The double-scan control genuinely cannot see a wrong root list: both passes see the same missing root and agree perfectly, and **two agreeing passes over the wrong frame is exactly what a correct scan looks like.** That control was built for an unstable filesystem and is blind to a wrong frame. The near-miss is also real: the thirteenth estate was only ever found by ADDING a second root, and had that root been misspelled rather than added, the census would have reported twelve with the same confidence and the same green control.

What was wrong was the claim that devbin does nothing about it. It does.

## Proposed Fix -- half 1 declined as unnecessary, half 2 LANDED

1. **A root that does not exist is REFUSED, not skipped.** Not taken, and not needed: the census already names an absent root as absent rather than dropping it. A hard `die` would additionally break the legitimate case of a root list carrying a path that is absent on this machine and present on another.

2. **The default root list is out of date.** **DONE.** `$HOME/Dropbox/Geodica/_tools` was removed as a default and the reason is recorded in place at `bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:44-66`: that estate moved to `$HOME/Devel/prj/Gtools`, and a second machine-specific path should never have been a default when `DEVBIN_FLEET_ROOTS` already existed as the override. Before the removal, every `bin/.devbin/manifest.sha256` under `$HOME` was enumerated to confirm no estate was lost by narrowing the frame.
